title: Senior Identity Security Engineer
description: <p><strong>Scopely </strong>is looking for a <strong>Senior Identity Security Engineer</strong> to join our Information Security team on a remote basis or hybrid basis if located in Barcelona.  This is a hands-on engineer who will build identity controls that reduce excessive privilege and protect critical operations. You will improve access across employee, player, business partner, and non-human identities by building AI-native identity workflows: agentic systems that handle provisioning, access reviews, and remediation within explicit guardrails, with humans approving what matters. Your work will protect the identities and access that support Scopely’s critical business processes, including essential enterprise functions and game operations.  This is a highly technical, hands-on role for someone who can operate across AWS, GCP, Okta, AWS IAM Identity Center, Zero Trust access models, identity governance workflows, and modern AI-enabled engineering environments, while building scalable identity systems through Infrastructure as Code, workflow orchestration, and automation-first security engineering.</p> <p><strong>What You Will Do</strong></p> <p><strong>Reduce identity attack surface and privilege</strong></p> <ul> <li>Reduce standing and excessive access with least-privilege roles, just-in-time and time-bound elevation, and automated access reviews.</li> <li>Build repeatable identity and access workflows that make onboarding, approvals, role changes, reviews, and offboarding consistent, traceable, and timely.</li> <li>Govern non-human identities, including service accounts, workload identities, CI/CD identities, API credentials, and AI agents and their tool integrations: inventory them, assign owners, replace long-lived secrets with short-lived or federated credentials, and rotate or revoke on a schedule and on signal.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Strengthen identity protection and resilience</strong></p> <ul> <li>Protect access to critical business processes and systems with phishing-resistant authentication (passkeys/FIDO2), device trust and posture signals, tightly controlled privileged access, and prompt revocation of suspicious sessions or compromised credentials.</li> <li>Threat-model identity platforms, integrations, and access paths to identify exploitable trust relationships, privilege escalation, and credential misuse. </li> <li>Build identity telemetry and response workflows to detect risky sign-ins, privilege changes, credential misuse, and compromised integrations. </li> <li>Design and test break-glass and recovery procedures for identity services and cloud access so teams can regain secure access during an outage or compromise.</li> <li>Extend the same patterns to player and partner identities where security owns the controls: platform identity federation (Apple, Google, Steam, console), account linking and recovery, external and vendor access, and defenses against account takeover and credential stuffing.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Build AI-native identity services</strong></p> <ul> <li>Build and operate reusable identity controls and services using infrastructure as code, APIs, scripting, and delivery pipelines. Apply code review, testing, drift detection, and audit trails so that every change, whether made by an engineer or an agent, is safe to deploy and easy to investigate.</li> <li>Design and build multi-agent workflows that surface identity risk, run access attestations, and triage and remediate access issues end to end. Engineer the harness those agents run in: scoped tools and permissions, curated context and data access, evals and test cases, orchestration between agents, and observability, so agent behavior is predictable, reviewable, and improvable.</li> <li>Treat agents as identities. Give every agent and MCP integration its own scoped credentials, least-privilege permissions, and bounded data access; validate inputs and outputs; log every action; and require human approval for changes that touch privileged access or production.</li> <li>Work with game and platform stakeholders to adopt shared identity patterns. Measure progress through reduced standing privilege, stale access, and unmanaged identities, and less manual work.</li> <li>Produce audit-ready evidence for access reviews, privileged access, and lifecycle events as a byproduct of the workflows rather than a separate project.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You Bring</strong></p> <ul> <li>5+ years of experience in IAM, or identity-focused cloud/security engineering, including hands-on ownership of production identity controls in complex environments.</li> <li>Strong experience with Okta or a comparable workforce identity platform and AWS/GCP IAM, as well as federation and provisioning protocols such as SAML, OIDC, OAuth, and SCIM.</li> <li>Production experience building, testing, and operating identity services or automation using Terraform or comparable infrastructure as code, Python, Go, or TypeScript., APIs, version control, and CI/CD.</li> <li>Strong knowledge of least privilege, just-in-time privileged access, identity lifecycle and governance, authentication controls, and non-human or workload identity risk.</li> <li>Experience threat-modeling identity architectures, integrations, and access paths, and driving remediation with service owners.</li> <li>Hands-on experience building AI-native workflows: systems where agents carry out multi-step work end to end, designed from the start around what agents can be trusted to do and where humans approve. Using a coding assistant does not count.</li> <li>Working fluency with harness engineering and multi-agent development: defining tools and permissions, scoping context and data, writing evals, orchestrating specialized agents, and instrumenting agent runs so failures are diagnosable, plus the judgment to keep those systems inside least-privilege boundaries.</li> <li>Ability to lead technical work from design through deployment and operations, and explain identity risks and implementation choices to stakeholders.</li> <li>Experience with identity governance, privileged access, or cloud entitlement tooling, or having built the equivalent in-house.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Nice-to-have</strong></p> <ul> <li>Consumer identity (CIAM) at scale, Kubernetes workload identity, detection engineering or SIEM experience, Okta or cloud security certifications, gaming or live-service experience.</li> </ul> <p><strong><br><br></strong></p><div class="content-conclusion"><p> </p> <h3>About Scopely</h3> <p>Scopely is a leading video game and global interactive entertainment company, home to many of the world’s most beloved and enduring experiences, including two of the most successful mobile games of all-time “MONOPOLY GO!” and “Pokémon GO,” along with “Stumble Guys,” “Star Trek™ Fleet Command,” “MARVEL Strike Force,” “WWE Champions,” the Scrabble® franchise, “Yahtzee® With Buddies,” and many others. Across mobile, web, PC, and console, Scopely creates, develops, publishes, and live-operates one of the most diversified and award-winning portfolios in the games industry — bringing hundreds of millions of players together through a shared love of play.</p> <p>Founded in 2011, Scopely is powered by its exceptional team — including thousands of world-class gamemakers around the globe, a distinctive tenet-driven culture, and its proprietary technology platform, Playgami. Together, these strengths have fueled Scopely’s position as the #1 mobile games company in the U.S. and #2 globally, generating more than $10 billion in lifetime revenue. Whether building global sensations like “MONOPOLY GO!” from the ground up, or expanding through strategic acquisitions, including the FoxNext, GSN, and Scopely Explore games businesses — Scopely consistently delivers experiences players love today and return to for years to come.</p> <p>Recognized multiple times as one of the "100 Most Influential Companies in the World" by TIME magazine and one of Fast Company's "World's Most Innovative Companies" and “Best Workplaces for Innovators,” Scopely believes that video games can be a force for good — creating meaningful connections, vibrant communities, and making life better through play.</p> <p>Scopely has global operations and partners across four continents in more than a dozen countries worldwide. For more information, visit: <a href="https://www.scopely.com/">https://www.scopely.com/</a>. </p> <p>Notice to Candidates: Scopely will never request payment or financial information during the application or hiring process. Please apply only through our official <a href="http://scopely.com">website</a> and verify that all Talent Partner communications come from an email address ending in @<a href="http://scopely.com">scopely.com</a>.</p> <p>Should you have any questions or encounter any fraudulent requests/emails/websites, please immediately contact ----- Our job applicant privacy policies are available here: <a href="https://www.scopely.com/en/job-applicant-privacy-notice-for-ca-residents">California Privacy Notice</a> and <a href="https://www.scopely.com/en/eea-and-uk-job-applicant-privacy-notice">EEA/UK Privacy Notice</a>.</p> <p>Employment at Scopely is based solely on a person's merit and qualifications. description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong>About WPP Media</strong></p> <p>WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. Connected through WPP Open and powered by Open Intelligence, clients see exactly where, how, and why their media investment is working.</p> <p>For more information, visit <a href="wppmedia.com">wppmedia.com</a>.</p></div><p></p> <p><strong>3623 - Director, Planning - UK</strong></p> <p><strong>Role Summary and Impact</strong></p> <p>We are recruiting for a Business Director who is an exceptional and driven media planner, to join our Connections Planning team working on the Ford account.</p> <p>We work in a unique ‘full service’ model meaning that the media teams collaborate closely with creative and account management teams within the Ford agency structure (primarily working with VML and WPP Production).</p> <p>Therefore we foster a fully integrated team approach across media, creative and client, working together across the agency and client locations - Ford’s Dunton office (a short taxi from Shenfield on the Elizabeth Line - travel costs are covered) when required, balanced with working together in WPP Rose Court London with creative and social teams.</p> <p>Your role, as a Business Director, will report to the Planning Lead, with support from the EVP, Clients, and will be focused on leading a team to deliver the planning and account management for Ford of Britain, across both Personal Vehicles and Commercial Vehicles. You will get the opportunity to design exciting, award-winning campaigns as well as work with channel specialists to make those plans a reality. This involves everything from defining the approach to audience, designing the connections plan across both brand & performance using all relevant touchpoints as well as advising on media innovation and measurement. We have strong inter-agency relationships, working closely with creative, PR & experiential and influencer agencies and enjoying senior client exposure. We have a very strong relationship with the client and are often seen as an extension of their team. Mindshare work on the Ford account globally, and whilst this role is UK specific there is a lot of collaboration between the teams.</p> <p>The remit also includes working in an integrated team leading on ESOP planning (earned, shared, owned and paid), collaborating closely with the creative team (VML) as well as the social team (WPP Production).</p> <p>You will be expected to demonstrate experience and knowledge in:</p> <ul> <li>Excellent stakeholder management with both clients and agency alike</li> <li>Ability to work with clients to ensure the brief is right with clear and measurable objectives in place</li> <li>An ability to think and work ‘audience first’, translating audience insight into actionable audiences </li> <li>Specify how to build and target audiences in addressable and non-addressable media and validate the approach to ensure that the defined audience can be reached at the scale required</li> <li>Designing an approach that outlines how and where we will connect with defined audiences in media</li> <li>Leading ESOP planning (earned, shared, owned and paid) within an integrated team</li> <li>Designing the connections ecosystem & plan, working closely and collaboratively with channel specialists </li> <li>Day to day management of campaigns as a key liaison between clients and channel specialists </li> <li>Designing measurement & testing framework to inform as well as measure and optimise the campaigns</li> <li>Line management of planning team within account structure</li> <li>Responsibilities to the planning department as senior member of the team, contributing to Business Director board meetings and leading work streams. </li> </ul> <p><strong>Skills and Experience</strong></p> <p>At WPP Media, we believe in the power of our culture and our people. In this role it will be critical to embrace WPP & WPP Media’s shared core values:</p> <ul> <li>Be <strong>Extraordinary</strong> by <em>Leading Collectively</em> to <em>Inspire transformational Creativity.</em></li> <li>Create an <strong>Open</strong> environment by<em> Balancing People and Client Experiences</em> by <em>Cultivating Trust</em>.</li> <li>Lead <strong>Optimistically</strong> by <em>Championing Growth</em> <em>and Development</em> to <em>Mobilize the Enterprise</em>.</li> </ul> <p>The specific attitudes and behaviours expected or this role are that:</p> <ul> <li>You show a passion for media and the industry with knowledge of the main trends that help to inform your thinking and output. </li> <li>You have clear opinions and an understanding of what makes a great media campaign - tangibly prove your plans are aimed at achieving excellence in planning craft.</li> <li>You can create a holistic measurement framework that is relevant for the brand and every campaign (setting KPIs, methods i.e., which tool/system, necessary tracking) and plans for adaptation/optimisation).  </li> <li>You must have extensive experience leading senior client relationships, managing all agency teams, leading and delivering client projects and tackling challenging conversations.</li> <li>You are an excellent team player taking the responsibility for working in a collaborative, inclusive way to allow specialists to contribute.</li> <li>You demonstrate a high degree of organisation that leads to successfully managing workflow for self and more junior members of the team.</li> <li>You are open-minded, flexible and embracing of agile ways of working.</li> </ul> <p><strong>The Ideal Candidate</strong></p> <p>As Business Director you will be responsible for the leadership and delivery of best-in-class planning and implementation. </p> <ul> <li>You will have a strong desire to deliver innovative and effective work both reactively (in response to briefs), and proactively (spotting those opportunities for insight and innovation outside of briefs). </li> <li>We expect our Business Directors to show a breath of understanding of media channels, as well as in-depth and speciality understanding in how to discuss the present and future role each channel plays as part of a comms strategy. </li> <li>Strong people management skills.</li> <li>Collaborative both in the day-to-day account role and across the planning department.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Life at WPP Media & Benefits</strong></p> <p>Our passion for shaping the next era of media includes investing in our employees to help them do their best work, and we’re just as committed to employee growth as we are to responsible media investment. description: Who We Are AI is changing how software gets built. Code production is becoming a commodity. The focus is shifting from writing code to specifying, orchestrating, verifying, and governing change – and the toolchain is the new constraint. We are at the center of this shift. title: Software Engineer, New Grad
description: Our Global Structure Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team. Software Engineer, New Grad Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation and growth drive everything we do. Our Engineering teams tackle complex technical challenges across a global, three-sided marketplace, building and scaling systems that serve millions of customers, riders and partners every day. From real-time logistics to resilient infrastructure and marketplace optimisation, we design, build and operate technology that powers Deliveroo's growth at scale. We're looking for a Software Engineer to join our London team. In this role, you'll help us build the future of on-demand delivery, contributing to the services that power our global marketplace. Get to know our Engineering team — what drives us, how we work, and what you can expect. What You'll Be Doing You'll be joining a high-impact engineering team at our London headquarters. As a New Grad, you will work on production systems that impact millions of users, supported by a world-class team of engineers. Here's what your day-to-day might look like: Ship high-quality code: Improve code structure and contribute to the architecture of services using languages like Go, Ruby, Python, or Scala. Own your features: Take ownership of specific pieces of work, assisting with design, technical implementation, and influencing your team's roadmap. Operational excellence: Aim to simplify the maintenance and health of production systems, ensuring operational readiness and visibility. Collaborate cross-functionally: Build relationships with other engineering teams to identify collaboration opportunities and solve complex marketplace problems. Grow through mentorship: Benefit from the support of senior colleagues while eventually supporting the growth of your peers through code reviews and knowledge sharing. What You'll Need to Thrive Our ideal candidate will bring strong expertise in some of these areas and curiosity to grow in others: Foundational Knowledge: A degree in Computer Science or a related technical field (graduated within the last year). Software Craftsmanship: Pride in writing readable, well-designed, and thoroughly tested software. Technical Curiosity: Experience writing web-based applications in any language and a strong interest in learning our stack (Go, Ruby/Rails, Python, Scala, or Rust). Data Fundamentals: Familiarity with relational databases (such as PostgreSQL or MySQL). Problem Solving: A proven ability to break down complex logistical or technical problems into manageable software solutions. Right to Work: Applicants must be authorised to work in the U.K. to be considered for this position. Why Join Us? At Deliveroo, you'll do work that matters—solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that's constantly evolving. We work continuously, proactively watching, delivering, and questioning whether the signal is real, acting as "first responders" to surprising deviations from expectation and using what we learn to drive faster, better decision-making for the business at large. Our work spans the full stack of analytics: from the warehouse models that make metrics trustworthy, to the monitoring systems that catch problems early, to the reports and dashboards that make performance visible, to the deep-dive investigations that explain what the numbers mean and what we should do about it. title: Principal Machine Learning Engineer GAIA
description: Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve. We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that. Here’s what this particular role covers. 🛠️ About our Simulation Teams You'll be joining the Simulation team (Simulation Evaluation & Validation), working on Gaia — Wayve's world model. Gaia is trained on large-scale driving video to predict future frames from past context, functioning as a simulator that generates synthetic scenarios and operates in closed loop with the driving model itself. The team partners closely with Research, Applications, Core Simulation Engineering, and Cloud/Infrastructure to turn model improvements into measurable downstream impact on the driving stack. 🧠 Your day-to-day Own and lead parts of large-scale training for Gaia (language- or video-style training at scale), from experimentation through productionised training runs. Contribute to and influence model architecture decisions — not just applying existing models. Partner across sub-teams: Research (model development), Applications (adapting models to use cases), Core Simulation Engineering, and Cloud/Infrastructure. Translate product and evaluation needs into model improvements (e.g. better long-horizon prediction, scenario generation quality, failure-case coverage). Mentor and set technical direction, raising the engineering and research quality bar across the team. 🧩 What you’ll be working on Leading and executing Gaia's post-training and closed-loop pipeline — fine-tuning and aligning the world model through post-training experimentation and targeted data curation. Pushing Gaia's autoregressive generation towards longer, more stable rollouts, and making the model deployment-ready (inference time and reliability included). Contributing to broader model architecture and training-strategy decisions where they intersect with pre- and post-training and the application layer. Partnering closely with research, applications, simulation engineering, and cloud/infrastructure teams to translate post-training improvements into measurable downstream impact. Providing technical leadership through mentorship, review, and setting high engineering/research standards. 🙌 You should apply if Essential: You have hands-on experience post-training/fine-tuning large-scale models (language, video, or other foundation models). You have experience with world models, autoregressive generation, and long-horizon generation. You have experience with diffusion/flow models and a solid understanding of 3D vision. You have a strong understanding of model architecture and can contribute meaningfully to architectural/training decisions. You have strong hands-on engineering skills with modern ML stacks (e.g. PyTorch), including debugging and performance/reliability-minded development. You have 5+ years of relevant industry experience (advanced degrees are valued, but depth of applied experience matters more). Desirable: Experience with inference optimisation or deploying large models under latency/compute constraints. Experience improving data/training pipelines and working across infrastructure constraints (distributed training, efficiency, reliability). Proven technical leadership — tech lead ownership, mentoring, or setting direction across an area. 🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement. More about Wayve: 🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines. Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility. How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working: Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives. 🔍 The Interview Process: Our process is clear and respectful of your time: Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins) Competency Interviews (Programming/Pytorch debugging and hiring manager interview; 2 hours total) Deep-dive technical interviews (Systems & domain-specific interviews; 3 hours total) Final interview : Mission & values alignment (45 mins). We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability. What’s in it for you (Location dependant): 💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually 📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve ✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable ✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs 📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth 🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more A quick, honest note before you apply. Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one. If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you. This team backs the visionary builders transforming Airwallex into a generational financial company, sharing the journey of product development and sales alongside our business partners. You’ll help shape a global licensing footprint most fintechs wish they had, while making sure our brand and data architecture stay best-in-class for customers entering the agentic economy and ready for its regulatory demands. The hard part is helping the business move fast on product, revenue, and new-market expansion without compromising the regulatory discipline that protects the moat. It’s a team for lawyers, strategists, and licensing specialists with commercial instincts, sharp judgment, and an obsession with customer-first outcomes. You will build strong relationships with business teams and develop a deep understanding of the business environment. When you don't know the answer, you'll know how to obtain it and explain it to business partners. This dynamic role is ideal for someone who enjoys wearing multiple hats and solving complex issues for our internal and external partners. You are detail oriented, willing to take on challenges and change, obsessively curious and intellectually honest. You thrive on taking action and delivering impactful results, and you aim to inspire and be inspired. Experience in fintech or payments is welcome, as is a demonstrated passion for mastering something new. Relevant subject-matter expertise may include knowledge of payments, card networks and banking. This role is based in Amsterdam or London, 3 days a week in the office. Responsibilities: Serve as a dedicated thought partner to our Strategic Partnership team, supporting negotiations on complex and novel agreements with some of our most important strategic partners and helping shape deals that drive Airwallex's global growth. title: Senior Full-Stack Software Engineer
description: ABOUT US At Heim, we are reinventing how healthcare is delivered. We believe that healthcare is best delivered in the home of patients, and that we are at the cusp of a systemic shift away from hospital based care. Our mission is to expand access to in-person clinical care at home by empowering community nurses with technology that makes care delivery more efficient. We have created an AI native ecosystem that optimises the complex scheduling involved in delivering community based care, and are on track to automate every non clinical touchpoint for nurses. To date, our technology has powered our network of 400+ practitioners to deliver c. 30K appointments, and we have shown that our algorithms bring down the cost of at-home visits by c.35% whilst freeing up valuable time for care in doing so. We are growing fast and our ambitions are big – with new international markets on the roadmap, and strong investor backing. Our aim is to create the most productive, AI-enabled distributed clinical workforce working at the intersection of public and private health.By joining Heim, you will play a pivotal role in building the infrastructure that puts clinical care in the home. WHAT IT'S LIKE TO WORK AT HEIM We are reinventing how healthcare is delivered. Here are the things that shape your day-to-day: Meaningful problems – we build systems that improve how organisations understand and care for people. The work is complex, applied, and grounded in real-world patient impact High standards, low ego – you’ll work alongside thoughtful engineers, clinicians, and operators who care about clarity and good judgement Speed with intent – we move quickly but deliberately. Clear ownership, evidence-based decisions, outcomes over output Simple, elegant solutions – we have a strong bias towards code that is easy to reason about, hard to break, and built to outlast the sprint it was born in Direct access to founders – you’ll have visibility into and input on the direction of the company WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE DIFFERENT This is a full-stack TypeScript role in the truest sense – you will own problems across the entire system, from UI to infrastructure. AI isn’t a feature here; it’s a first principle. We expect you to use agentic coding tools fluently (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor) and to be building your own views on where agentic workflows can meaningfully improve what we ship. You’ll be working on systems where the stakes are real: scheduling errors affect patient care, data quality issues affect clinical decisions, and downtime has consequences. That context sharpens every technical choice you make. WHAT YOU'LL DO Design and build product features end-to-end across the Heim tech stack – owning them from first principles to production Architect and implement AI-powered workflows: scheduling optimisation, practitioner dispatch, clinical data enrichment, and agentic referral automations that reduce manual touchpoints for nurses Own the full lifecycle of features – from TypeScript frontend through to backend services, infrastructure, deployment pipelines, and testing – without relying on separate DevOps or QA teams to close the loop Build and maintain the APIs, services, and data models that underpin clinical operations – with the reliability and auditability a regulated environment demands Collaborate with our product and clinical ops teams to translate ambiguous real-world problems into working software Make pragmatic trade-offs between speed and quality, and advocate clearly when the trade-off isn’t acceptable Contribute to the architecture and infrastructure decisions that will shape the platform as we scale to NHS Trusts across the UK and into new markets Leave the codebase better than you found it – improving performance, clarity, and resilience as part of everyday delivery You won’t get perfectly specified tickets. You’ll be trusted to think, decide, and ship. HOW WE WORK Small team, fast loops, few layers – your decisions land fast and the feedback is real We operate a hybrid team set up, and value high quality in person time so you must be able to commute to our central London office Technical judgement is respected and expected – you’ll have a real voice in architectural decisions Disagreement is normal. Good ideas win, not hierarchical ones Strong bias toward execution: fewer meetings, clear ownership, and decisions grounded in evidence WHO THIS IS FOR You’re a senior full-stack engineer who acts like a founder. You take responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks. You’re comfortable roaming an unfamiliar part of the codebase when something needs fixing, and you’ll ask sharp clarifying questions before committing to an approach. You probably have: 6+ years building and owning production software in fast-moving environments Genuine full-stack capability – you’re not “mostly frontend” or “mostly backend”; you care about and can own the whole system Proven ability to own the full delivery lifecycle: frontend, backend, infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines, deployment, and testing – without handing off to separate DevOps or QA teams Active, fluent use of AI coding tools – Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot – not as novelty, but as default workflow Experience making data-sensitive engineering decisions: you instinctively ask about PII classification, schema flexibility, and audit requirements before you build A track record of shipping under ambiguity – you’ve taken a vague ask, formed a point of view, and delivered something that worked The judgement to know when to move fast and when to slow down Bonus if you have: Experience in regulated environments (healthcare, fintech, legal) and an understanding of what “good enough” looks like when data sensitivity is high Background building agentic or multi-step AI workflows in production A side project or personal tool built with AI – something that shows you’ve been hands-on with Cursor, Claude Code, or AI integrations outside of work Familiarity with NHS data standards, FHIR, or community care systems Infrastructure and cloud experience (GCP or equivalent) beyond the basics Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

description: About GetGround GetGround is the all-in-one platform for UK property investors, helping landlords find, finance, structure and manage buy-to-let investments, and prepare and file their tax returns. Investors around the world trust us with their companies, finances and property. Purpose of the role You will assist with the design and running of GetGround's data privacy and AI governance programmes day to day, working closely with the Senior Director - Legal, Risk & Compliance. You will advise teams, keep our compliance records current, handle rights requests and breaches, and build our AI governance framework so that the AI tools we use are lawful and well controlled. Data privacy responsibilities Advise teams on their obligations under the UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, PECR and the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025. Run the data privacy compliance programme to the DPO's assurance plan, covering policies, records of processing, retention, training and audits. Support business owners to complete DPIAs and keep the DPIA register. Deliver the data protection framework for Self Assessment and Making Tax Digital processing Review data-sharing, processor and partner agreements, including white-label partnerships, and international transfer arrangements. Handle subject access and other rights requests and data privacy complaints; prepare breach assessments with Information Security for the DPO's decision. Prepare data privacy evidence for partner due diligence. Deliver data privacy training and keep the Senior Director and business up to date on legal and regulatory changes AI governance responsibilities Build and maintain a register of AI systems and use cases, including third-party tools, with an owner and risk rating for each. Run risk assessments for new AI use cases, combined with DPIAs where personal data is involved, covering accuracy, bias, transparency and human oversight. Maintain the Responsible Use of AI Policy and governance framework, and deliver AI training. Advise on safeguards for automated decision-making, including the right to human review. Review AI vendors and model providers before onboarding, and keep a log of AI incidents, tracking each to closure. Prepare reports to the Risk & Compliance Committee on data privacy and AI governance. In addition to the above, the role will involve contributing to a number of strategic growth projects across the business and collaborating closely with other members of the Legal, Risk & Compliance team to build a scalable and comprehensive approach to managing data privacy and AI risk, enabling proper governance, oversight and streamlined legal, risk and compliance processes. Skills and experience Essential Expert, current knowledge of UK data protection law and ICO guidance. Working knowledge of AI governance, including ICO guidance on AI and data protection, the EU AI Act, and frameworks such as ISO/IEC 42001 or the NIST AI Risk Management Framework. At least five years in a data privacy role in a company, such as data protection manager or privacy lead, with experience of governing AI or automated decision-making. Experience in financial services, fintech, proptech or another regulated, data-heavy business. Track record of running DPIAs and AI risk assessments, handling incidents and managing rights requests at volume. Ability to turn legal requirements into practical, commercial advice, and the confidence to challenge and execute on tasks within tight timeframes Desirable IAPP CIPP/E or CIPM, or the BCS Practitioner Certificate in Data Protection; IAPP AIGP; a legal qualification. Experience of data protection in tax, accountancy or HMRC agent services, including Making Tax Digital. Knowledge of AML/KYC processes, FCA expectations and EU, Hong Kong or Singapore data protection rules. What we are building: The first end-to-end real estate investment offering - making the dream of owning real estate more accessible to everyone globally. description: About Us: Fireworks is the platform for specialized intelligence, enabling companies to build, train, and serve AI models tailored to their own data, workflows, and products. Today, Fireworks is a Series D company valued at $17.5 billion, bringing together an ambitious, collaborative team that's building the future of enterprise AI. The Role: As an Applied Machine Learning Engineer, you are the technical owner of a customer engagement. This is what is globally known as the Forward Deployed Engineer role; at Fireworks in EMEA it carries the AMLE title. You embed with a small number of accounts, work in their environment, and own whatever stands between them and production on Fireworks: the model, the serving path, the integration, the performance. You scope the work before signature and deliver what you scoped. Depth over breadth: few accounts, owned end to end. What we value most is first principles thinking: reasoning about unfamiliar problems from the ground up rather than from playbooks. You will be evaluated on this directly in the interview process, and strength here can outweigh gaps elsewhere in your background. Four Spikes: Software engineering. You ship production systems and are comfortable dropped into an unfamiliar codebase or a customer environment with a deadline. Backend and systems depth, strong Python plus at least one systems language, and fluency with AI-assisted and agentic engineering as a core part of how you build. Machine learning. You take open models and make them better on a customer's task: SFT, LoRA and other parameter-efficient methods, reinforcement learning (RLHF, RLVR), distillation. Just as important, you design evaluations that reflect the real task and let them drive training decisions, and you know when fine-tuning is not the answer. Infrastructure and performance. You know your GPUs: memory bandwidth, kernels, parallelism, what utilization numbers actually mean. Serving and inference optimization: quantization, speculative decoding, batching, KV cache behavior, latency vs throughput tradeoffs, multi-GPU and multi-node serving, capacity planning. You can take a deployment that works and make it fast and economical, and reason about where the bottleneck is before touching a profiler. Customer engagement. You want to be in the room. The point of this role is creating specialized intelligence for each customer: the best model for their task, their data, their constraints. That takes real interest in the customer's problem, not just the technical one. Exceptional here looks like founder energy with customers; the floor is genuine appetite to embed, explain, and own outcomes with them. Key Responsibilities: Own Engagements: Take customer deployments from scoping through production, as the single accountable technical owner. Embed: Work directly inside customer teams; understand their domain, data, and constraints well enough to make decisions they trust. Train and Tune: Run fine-tuning and post-training work where the engagement needs it, from data to evaluation to a model serving in production. Optimize: Drive serving performance and cost on Fireworks: model choice, deployment shape, and inference optimization. Scope Honestly: Assess what is achievable before we commit, and inherit what you scope. Product Signal: Feed what customers need back to product and engineering, with enough precision to be actionable. Minimum Qualifications: Spikes in two or all three areas. For the ML spike: formal training (PhD, PhD in progress, or a strong MSc) and experience post-training LLMs specifically. For the infrastructure spike: experience with GPU infrastructure, distributed serving, or inference engines. Founder or founding engineer experience. Experience in a startup or fast-paced environment. Why Fireworks? Solve Hard Problems: Tackle challenges at the forefront of AI infrastructure, from low-latency inference to scalable model serving. Build What’s Next: Work with bleeding-edge technology that impacts how businesses and developers harness AI globally. Ownership & Impact: Join a fast-growing, passionate team where your work directly shapes the future of AI—no bureaucracy, just results. Learn from the Best: Collaborate with world-class engineers and AI researchers who thrive on curiosity and innovation. Fireworks AI is an equal-opportunity employer. description: <div class="content-intro"><h2><span data-sheets-root="1">About Wolt</span></h2> <p><span data-sheets-root="1">At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. So, if you’re a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.</span></p></div><p><strong>Strategy & Operations Senior Manager, Consumer</strong></p> <p><strong>About the Team</strong></p> <p>The EMEA Consumer Strategy & Operations team drives efficient customer growth across Deliveroo and Wolt. description: Strategy & Operations (3-6 YoE) London, 5x days per week in-office Vega is looking for multi-disciplinary A players who have what it takes to build a business from the ground up. We hire people who are already high-performers in MBB or finance/investing, but still have the itch to do more. This role will sit in the CEO Office, reporting to the Head of Strategy & Growth, working across the highest strategic priorities in the business. About Vega Vega is transforming the way private markets operate. Alternative asset management is one of the most influential forces in the global economy, with over $20TN in assets today. Over the next five years, the industry is set to grow 3x, but GPs are facing challenges around their ability to handle the investment flows that are coming in. GPs have been completely underserved by innovation, particularly on the investor relations side. Vega built the industry’s first AI-native operating system, where all client work gets done - from the start of an investor’s journey to its end. We are rethinking how work gets done in private markets from first principles: the opportunity is big, but it’s also niche, high-stakes, and difficult to get right. Who we are We are still at the beginning of our journey. Vega was founded by former investors at Elliott and KKR, and built by talent from the world’s leading technology and financial services firms - including Trade Republic, Revolut, Goldman Sachs, BCG, and more. We have raised $30M so far, with the backing of Apollo, Motive Partners, and 60+ senior executives from the industry. Today, we have over $300B AUM and 30,000 users on the platform, and we have much more left to do. How we do it Vega is a fast-growing startup. We want to make this a career-accelerating place for people with the ambition to build something big. If the below sounds appealing, it could be for you: We do not seek consensus. You will be expected to voice opinions and take initiative. Vega's best people do not wait to be told what to do before finding solutions to problems they have spotted. We believe bureaucracy is the killer of progress. We are focused on creating the minimum viable process to operate with quality at speed. We prioritise talent over tenure. There is no promise of progression without performance – we assess and reward people on impact above all else. We iterate fast. We make decisions amid ambiguity and with imperfect information, and we strive to balance committing to a hypothesis with iterating at low ego. We play to win. title: Senior Engineer - Platform & Tooling
description: Who is Atominvest Atominvest is the operating system for modern private markets asset managers. Our modular, flexible SaaS technology underpins key investor- and portfolio-management workflows. Our customers are sophisticated private equity, growth equity, and private credit firms managing billions in assets globally. We aim to deliver ongoing high-quality outcomes for them through a long-term partnership mindset. At Atominvest, you’ll be working on something very exciting: the future of work, investments and sustainability/ ethical investing for the world’s best investors and delivering a positive impact through this. Based on the growth we are experiencing, we think we’re on to something big. It won’t be easy. Joining a scale up business is an amazing and rewarding challenge, pushing well beyond the boundaries of natural growth cycles. You’ll move quicker than feels comfortable and be brilliant at continually re-prioritizing what must get done to keep Atominvest growing year over year at the pace of the best SaaS companies on the planet. We’ve gone from zero to ten, now we’re looking to go from ten to one hundred! About the role Hi, I'm Thomas, VP Engineering at Atominvest. This is the hire I'm most excited about, so I wanted to tell you about it myself. You'll own the platform our clients run on and build the AI development harness our engineers work in day to day. That work runs from infrastructure to application code, so we're looking for an experienced engineer with breadth across both, and depth in at least one. Together, it's what lets a small, lean team, working alongside AI agents, ship like a much bigger one. By platform, we mean everything our product and our engineers stand on: infrastructure, security, test automation, developer experience, and the agent pipelines that run through all of them. It's a broad, hands-on role. You'll write infrastructure as code for a new service one day and address network vulnerabilities the next, then enhance our AI development harness and release a new feature, all within the same month. You might be a platform engineer who loves shipping product, or a full-stack engineer who has run serious production infrastructure. Either works. As deployments grow more complex, the team needs your depth in infrastructure and distributed systems. You'll strengthen the architecture and make the design decisions the platform will rest on for years. Those decisions should leave room to grow, because future products may bring much larger volumes of data than we handle today. It has to stay dependable while we do it. Our software needs to be available around the clock, every day of the year, and data integrity is critical. Our clients use Atominvest to report to their own investors, so a wrong number matters as much as an outage. Security, reliability and audit-readiness matter too. If you enjoy getting those right without slowing everything else down, you'll find plenty of fun things to work on. The machine that builds the product We're becoming AI-native. Agents do more and more of the mechanical work of writing code, and engineers build the machine that builds the product: the architecture, the specs, the limits agents work within, and the evals that tell us whether their output is right. I think that moves an engineer's leverage upstream. When code is cheap, the scarce things are judgement and understanding. Which problem is worth solving? What does good look like for the person using it? Is the output actually right? Did what we shipped help? The best engineers I've worked with always solved the end problem, with code as the medium. Now that's most of the job. That's why product and user understanding sit at the centre of how we work. An engineer who knows our clients' workflows can point agents at the right problem and spot when the result is subtly wrong. Without that, agents just build the wrong thing faster. Your part is the AI development harness that makes this safe. That means sandboxed environments with synthetic data, scoped and audited access to logs and alerts, and evals and validation gates in CI. It also means firm lines, enforced by tooling, that keep production deploys and secrets in human hands, and client data out of reach of development agents. You'll also build the agent orchestration pipelines that run in three places: in how we build software, in AI workflows inside the product our clients use, and in the internal tools our implementation team uses to onboard and configure clients. What you'll do Build the machine that builds the product Most of your time goes here. Build our AI development harness. Self-service infrastructure, a reproducible development environment, and the sandboxes, guardrails and evals that let agents take on more of the work safely, with results we can measure. Automate quality. Build the QA automation pipeline: automated tests, validation gates and release checks that give us confidence in every change, including the ones agents write. Orchestrate agents across the business. Build pipelines that run agents reliably and safely in our product workflows and our internal implementation tools, not just in engineering. Own the platform Own our infrastructure. We're migrating to ECS. You'll strengthen our ECS architecture, see the move through in safe, reversible stages, bring every resource under infrastructure as code, and retire the old deployment model. Build security into the platform. Tenant-scoped credentials, per-tenant secrets, least-privilege access, and the audit trail that SOC 2 and our clients' security teams expect. Make production observable. Set up the monitoring, alerting and tracing we rely on, and build playbooks for on-call and incident response which is shared amongst the team. Work across the stack Make the application changes the harness needs, such as synthetic data, test hooks and the specs agents work from. Ship product. Pick up application work in TypeScript and React alongside the team. Over time, you'll learn the codebase as well as the platform it runs on. Grow the team around you. Write the design notes and runbooks, pair with and review the work of other engineers, and mentor those who want to grow into infrastructure, so the platform never depends on one person. Your first six months Get the first parts of "the machine" running, and show that they make the team faster without lowering quality. At the moment all of our end to end testing is done manually by our Product team. That's a massive manual overhead that bottlenecks our product development. You'll help build our AI-powered QA automation pipeline, so every change, whether a person or an agent wrote it, is tested automatically before it reaches clients. Strengthen the ECS architecture and complete the move with no disruption to clients. Get the platform fully into code, with tenant isolation and least privilege designed in. Put in place the monitoring and on-call foundations the team will build on. How you'll work You'll own this area rather than work through a ticket queue. You'll decide what to build and when it's good enough, write your decisions down so others can challenge them, and tell us when something isn't worth doing. You'll work closely with Product from the start of significant work, because the platform exists to serve clients and the engineers building for them. You and I will work together every day. We'll shape the technical direction together and think through the hard calls, and you'll have a direct line to every decision that affects your work. I'll back your judgement, and I'll expect you to push back when you think I'm wrong. This is an individual contributor role, but we expect you to multiply the team: leading different areas at different times, and delivering through others as well as through your own work. You'll probably enjoy this if You'd rather build a platform properly than keep patching one. You're product-minded. You've probably worked at a startup or scale-up, or even founded something yourself. Seeing your work out in the world, solving real problems, is what motivates you. You ask who a change is for before you ask how to build it. You already work this way. Agents write much of your code, and your time goes on design, specs and judging the output. You've built AI tooling for yourself, and probably for others on your team. You get satisfaction from making other engineers faster. You're comfortable writing Terraform, an API endpoint and an answer to a client's security questionnaire in the same week. You've been the person others come to with hard problems, and you've changed your mind publicly when the evidence said so. This probably isn't for you if You want a pure DevOps or SRE role. You want to manage people right now. These opportunities might exist in the future, but for now we're small, lean and as flat as possible. What you'll bring Very few people match every line. If most of this describes you, we'd like to hear from you. Deep, hands-on AWS. Several years running production workloads on ECS or EKS, with a solid grasp of IAM, networking and Lambda. Infrastructure as code as a habit , with Terraform or CloudFormation, including bringing existing hand-built resources under code. Scaling distributed systems. You've taken systems through real growth in load and data, and can teach others what you learnt. Single-tenant SaaS experience. You know the isolation trade-offs and how to keep one client's data and credentials away from another's. description: Project Tricorder — Clinical Infrastructure for Field Operations We're looking for a hands-on engineer to build two foundations of the Tricorder product: the evaluation harness and training data pipeline behind our AI models, and a clinical knowledge base grounded in tactical combat care, SNOMED CT and ICD-10. About Project Tricorder - https://www.tricorder-systems.com/ Most healthcare technology assumes a hospital: reliable power, connectivity and a clinician at a desk. Care increasingly happens somewhere else - in the field, in transit, in remote and contested environments, and in the critical minutes before a patient reaches a ward. Tricorder builds the deployable clinical infrastructure for that world: a rugged, self-contained hardware and software platform that lets clinical teams capture, monitor and act on patient data anywhere, even when the network or the grid can't be relied on. It is a dual-use venture serving defence medical and civilian pre-hospital care. Our prototype product is already in user testing. Edge AI sits at the core: multimodal language models that turn video, sensor data and clinical notes into patient records, drive predictions and inform data-driven learnings across deployments. To trust those models in the field, we need rigorous data and evaluation - that's where you come in. What you'll do You'll own two workstreams, working day to day with the founder and the FF build team. 1. Data pipeline and evaluation harness Build the data foundations that tell us whether our models are good enough for clinical use. Data labelling: design labelling schemas and guidelines, set up tooling, and run labelling with clinical input, including quality checks and inter-annotator agreement. title: Fractional Chief Medical Officer  - Tricorder Systems
description: Fractional Chief Medical Officer — Project Tricorder We're looking for a clinician who has served as a military medic to be Tricorder's clinical lead and the medical name behind the product. You'll shape clinical workflows, protect patient safety, help to roadmap clinical device regulation, giving the product credibility with clinicians, defence customers and investors. About Project Tricorder - https://www.tricorder-systems.com/ Most healthcare technology assumes a hospital: reliable power, connectivity and a clinician at a desk. But the moments that decide outcomes often happen elsewhere: at the point of injury, in transit, in remote and contested environments, and in the critical minutes before a patient reaches a ward. Tricorder is building deployable clinical infrastructure for that world. It's a rugged, self-contained hardware and software platform that lets clinical teams capture, monitor and act on patient data anywhere, even when the network or the grid can't be relied on. It's a dual-use venture serving defence medical first and civilian pre-hospital and humanitarian care next. Tricorder is being built inside Founders Factory's venture studio, with dedicated pre-seed investment and a six-month build programme. The founder, a former British Army officer, is in place, the founding engineer is incoming, and a few more team hires are underway. What you'll do You'll be Tricorder's senior clinical voice: the person who makes sure what we build works for a medic at the point of injury and keeps patients safe. Shape clinical workflows: map how casualties are assessed, treated, handed over and evacuated, from the point of injury through to definitive care. Turn that into product requirements, and test prototypes against real resuscitation and trauma scenarios. Protect patient safety: lead clinical risk management and act as (or help appoint) the Clinical Safety Officer under the NHS DCB0129 standard. Advise on the evidence needed for the medical device and regulatory pathway. Be the medical face of the product: put your clinical name to Tricorder. Represent it to defence medical services, NHS and ambulance trusts, humanitarian organisations and investors, and help the founder carry the clinical story in pitches and pilots. Open doors: use your network across defence medicine, the NHS and humanitarian response to secure clinical pilots, user testing and early design partners. Guide clinical evidence: help design pilots and early studies, and review clinical claims, protocols and terminology across the product and its AI features. Advise the team: be a sounding board for the founder and build team on clinical priorities. Help with clinical hiring as the company grows. Who you are Must-haves You've served as a military medic or doctor. This is non-negotiable. You know operational medicine first-hand, from point-of-injury care to the field hospital. A GMC-registered doctor with deep experience in resuscitation, trauma or emergency surgery, emergency medicine, or pre-hospital care. Still active clinically, whether as a reservist, in the NHS, or in humanitarian or disaster response. You're credible with senior defence medical leaders, NHS clinicians and investors, and comfortable being the named clinical lead for a product. You can turn clinical reality into clear, practical product decisions, and you're happy working with engineers and designers at startup pace. Nice to have Experience advising or working with medtech or health-tech startups, ideally as a CMO, clinical lead or advisor. Clinical Safety Officer training (DCB0129/DCB0160), or experience with medical device regulation (UKCA/CE, ISO 14971). Leadership roles in defence medical services, such as a clinical lead, medical director or command role. Experience with mass-casualty planning, deployed hospital care, or global health systems. Familiarity with clinical AI, data standards or digital health interoperability. Probably not the right fit if You haven't served in a military medical role. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar. Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes. 2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. Role overview Legora is looking for an Editorial Specialist to join our Communications team in London or Stockholm. This role will sit within the Editorial team and help shape how Legora shows up across social, editorial, and owned content channels.
